note: Sources for the desert rosettes added and revised in 0.9.94. Figures were read from the Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center (WFC), the Native Plant Society of Texas (NPSOT), the RHS, and San Marcos Growers (SMG, an archived catalog since the nursery closed). Missouri Botanical Garden (MBG) pages failed a certificate check when fetched, so MBG figures here come from search-result excerpts of its Plant Finder and are marked `excerpt`. Agaves and sotols state the rosette as heightIn, since their stalk is rare or ends the plant; yuccas, hesperaloes, beargrass and false aloe state the height in flower, except giant hesperaloe, whose fifteen-foot stalk is drawn above a rosette height (topScale). Sizes conflict badly between nurseries for every one of these plants, so `estimates` says which figure was chosen and why.

plants.estimates: WFC: leaves to about 18 in, flower stalk to about 4.5 ft, a 3-4 ft wide clump. heightIn is the stalk's usual height below that maximum. Zones unchanged from the existing record.

WFC: a 6 ft flowering stalk over 2-3 ft clumps, up to about 9 ft in bloom; native Long Island and PA south to FL and LA. MBG (excerpt): zone 5 to 10, 4-8 ft, spread 2-3 ft, stalk 5-8 ft, June to July. Bloom months [6,7] are MBG's, inside WFC's April-August.
MBG (excerpt): zone 4 to 10, 3-6 ft. Moved from soapweed yucca, where it was filed with no native range; it is a selection of a North American native.
MBG (excerpt): zone 4 to 9, 2-3 ft by 3-4 ft. Height in flower is left at the species' figure.

RHS: 1.5-2.5 m tall and wide, panicles to 2 m of nodding cream bells in late summer, H5. WFC: to about 15 ft in cultivation, blooms September-November, coastal dunes from NC to NE Florida. heightIn is the RHS upper height; zones 7-10 read from H5 (-15 to -10 C) and SMG's 'hardy to 0 F' for 'Variegata'. Bloom months [8,9,10] join RHS's late summer to WFC's fall.
SMG: 6-8 ft tall by 4-6 ft wide, cream marginal variegation that blushes red in the cold months, hardy to 0 F. Inherits the species' size.
RHS: 1-1.5 m by 1.5-2.5 m, mid-green centre broadly edged yellow, pink buds opening white, H5, AGM. heightIn and spread are the middle of those ranges.

SMG: 12-16 ft by 6-8 ft, hardy to about 0 F, white flowers in late spring, western Texas and Chihuahua and Coahuila. RHS: 2.5-4 m by 1.5-2.5 m, leaves 60-90 cm by 1.3-2.5 cm, H5. heightIn is 10 ft, between the two, for a plant that takes decades to reach the top of either. Zone 6 is a planning floor: SMG says 0 F (zone 7) and the plant is grown in colder gardens than that, so this is the one zone figure here not read from a page.
SMG: a blue-gray seedling selection by Sean Hogan of Cistus Nursery, same size as the species. RHS: silvery-blue leaves to 60 cm with thin yellow margins, H5.

WFC: leaves to 16 in, a 4-5 ft flowering stalk, greenish-white tubes May-August, MD to s. OH and s. MO south to FL and TX. MBG (excerpt): zone 6 to 9 (protected in 5), 3-6 ft, spread 3-4 ft, leaves 6-20 in long and 2 in wide, sometimes flecked red, sun to part shade. Spread 30 in is the rosette a 16 in leaf makes, not MBG's clump. Wikipedia files it as Agave virginica, its newer name.
WFC: leaves 2-3 ft, plum-coloured in winter, coral tubular flowers on arching pink stems to 5 ft. Only the winter leaf colour and the yellow inside of the flower changed.
SMG: 'Perpa', PP21,729; 2-3 ft tall and wide, wands to about 3 ft, red flowers early spring to late summer, recommended in USDA zones 6-10, sets no seed (so it draws no seed in fall).
SMG: 3-4 ft, stalks 5-9 ft that arch up and out, yellow flowers in mid-summer, hardy to at least 0 F. Height in flower left at the species' figure.

WFC: leaves to about 6 ft, flower spikes to about 15 ft, white and yellow flowers March-May, San Luis Potosi north to Val Verde County, Texas. heightIn is the foliage; the spike is drawn about twice that. Spread and zones are planning values from nursery listings (4-6 ft wide; zones mostly 7-10) since no page read gives either.
WFC: leaves to about 3 ft, flower stalk to about 15 ft, rising 10 ft above the rosette. Record unchanged; the drawing now carries the stalk at 2.2 times the rosette.

WFC: leaf cluster 1.5-2.5 ft, a 9-15 ft flower stalk with a 2-3 ft spike of yellowish flowers June-July, dark bluish-green leaves with evenly spaced spines. NPSOT: 2-3 ft by 3-4 ft. Zones 7-10 follow Woodlanders and most listings; neither page gives one.

WFC: up to about 30 in, leaves up to 4 ft long by 3/16 in wide with widely spaced tiny teeth, cream flowers in dense clusters that barely clear the foliage March-July, part shade, AZ, CO, NM, OK, TX. NPSOT: 1.5-3 ft by 3-4 ft, February-June. Zone 6 floor rests on its Colorado range and SNWA's 6a; other listings say 7.
SMG: 3-5 ft by 6-8 ft, hardy to at least 4-5 F, solitary (non-offsetting), cupped gray leaves with small teeth and a 1 in terminal spine. RHS: 1-1.5 m by 1.5-2.5 m, H3, Mexico, does not offset.
SMG: 3-4 ft by 3-4 ft (prose 2-5 by 3-6 ft), a near-turquoise selection by Sean Hogan of Cistus Nursery.
SMG: 2-3 ft by 3-4 ft, cold hardy to around 15 F (zone 8), broad, short, squared-off blue-gray leaves with reddish-brown teeth, native Durango to Zacatecas.
SMG: 1.5-2 ft by 2.5 ft, to around -20 F, narrower triangular gray leaves than A. parryi, often suckers into small colonies. Its native range in New Mexico and west Texas is the species' own.
